containmentMethod: resolve() then require the root to be a direct child of the identities parent, reject reparse points on the chain, and reject equality with the default root
ttyCheck: stdin.isatty() and stdout.isatty(), evaluated before any custody construction
manualConfirmation: CREATE IDENTITY <CODE>, code derived from profile name plus derived root, non-secret, printed on screen only
credentialSource: existing protected in-process prompt inside the canonical Python process
fixtureCredential: throwaway fixture passphrase inside the canonical test process only
fixtureRoots: throwaway LOCALAPPDATA redirected to a temporary directory, removed after each test
didAUnchangedMethod: sha256 of the opaque identity.dpapi ciphertext plus size/mtime, and of local-install.json, operator.json and nonces.json, captured before source work and re-compared after; DPAPI protect() is randomized so any rewrite changes the ciphertext digest
canonicalUnchangedSurfaces: service/local_init.py default root logic and single-root guard
limitations: DID B still does not exist. This phase landed and validated an enrollment entrypoint; it did not enrol anything real.
The fixture E2E used real Windows DPAPI with throwaway keys under a redirected LOCALAPPDATA. It proves namespace and DID separation, not that an enrolled second identity is safe to operate.
The TTY gate is a human-presence interlock. It stops unattended automation, not a determined local attacker already running as the same Windows user.
The confirmation phrase is a non-secret derived code. It prevents a mistyped or copy-pasted enrollment; it authenticates nobody.
No signature exists for any additional profile. A working signing path for a future DID B remains unproven and belongs to a later phase.
Two DIDs on this machine would remain ONE human operator: not two humans, not two organizations, not two economic counterparties, not evidence of payment, and not FLOP eligibility.
nextRecommendedAction: Human runs docs/PHASE3BC1B_HUMAN_ENROLLMENT.md in a normal PowerShell window, reports only the public DID and fingerprint, then Phase 3B.C1 is re-run to record DID B
